auth.description: Intercom access token sent as a bearer — an OAuth app token or a workspace access token
auth.name: intercom.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Which region this Intercom workspace is hosted in. Pick United States, European Union or Australia — Intercom assigns the region when the workspace is created and it does not change. If you are not sure, look at the URL you use Intercom at: app.intercom.com is the US region, app.eu.intercom.com the EU one and app.au.intercom.com the Australian one. A token issued for one region returns 401 against another, exactly as a revoked token would
config.label: Intercom region
config.name: host

description: Intercom contacts and conversations: read and create contacts, read a conversation, reply to it, and note it

operations.description: Get one Intercom contact by id — its role, email, name, custom attributes, tags and the companies it belongs to

params.description: The contact's Intercom id — a 24-character lowercase hexadecimal string such as `63a0979a5eeebeb3d8ba5be3`, not its email or your own external id
params.name: contact_id

avatar.description: `{type, image_url}` or null — an object, not a URL string

companies.description: The same wrapper shape — companies at `.data`

created_at.description: Unix seconds — an integer, not an ISO string

custom_attributes.description: The workspace's own attributes, keyed by name. Which keys exist is per workspace, so none is declared

external_id.description: Your own id for this person, or null. Intercom's identity model treats this and `email` as the two identifiers

has_hard_bounced.description: Their address bounced permanently; mail to it will not arrive

id.description: The 24-character Intercom id, which is what this operation takes

last_seen_at.description: Unix seconds of the last time Intercom saw this person, or null. This is the field that says whether a contact is live

location.description: Intercom's IP-derived guess: `{type, country, region, city}`

notes.description: The same wrapper shape — notes at `.data`

owner_id.description: The admin who owns the contact, or null

role.description: `user` for an identified person or `lead` for an unidentified visitor. A lead can be merged into a user later, which changes the id a flow should hold

signed_up_at.description: Unix seconds, or null for a contact that never signed up

tags.description: A PAGINATED WRAPPER, not an array: `{type, data, url, total_count, has_more}`. The tags are at `.data`, and `has_more` true means there are more than were returned

unsubscribed_from_emails.description: TRUE MEANS DO NOT EMAIL THIS PERSON. Check it before a flow sends anything

workspace_id.description: The workspace the contact belongs to — Intercom's app id

operations.description: Create an email-identified Intercom contact. A contact created here is visible to every teammate in the workspace and is counted against its contact quota; creating one twice creates two contacts unless the workspace deduplicates on email

params.description: `user` for an identified person or `lead` for an unidentified visitor. A lead is merged into a user if that person later signs up
params.name: role

params.description: The contact's email address, which is how this operation identifies them. Intercom does not verify it
params.name: email

created_at.description: Unix seconds — an integer, not an ISO string

id.description: The new contact's id — the only handle on the record this call created, and what a following note addresses

last_seen_at.description: Null until Intercom sees the person

signed_up_at.description: Null on a contact created this way

tags.description: The paginated wrapper shape, empty on a new contact

operations.description: Get one conversation by id, with its state, the contacts on it and its message parts in Intercom's default rendering

params.description: The conversation's Intercom id — a decimal string such as `123`, as it appears in the inbox URL
params.name: conversation_id

admin_assignee_id.description: The assigned admin, or null when unassigned

ai_agent_participated.description: Whether Intercom's own AI agent replied in this conversation, which is worth knowing before a second automation replies too

contacts.description: The customers on the conversation, as `{type, contacts: […]}` — a wrapper, not an array

conversation_parts.description: THE MESSAGES, nested twice: `{type, conversation_parts: […], total_count}`. Each part carries `part_type` (`comment`, `note`, `assignment`, `close`), `body` as HTML, `author` and `created_at`. Only a page of them is returned — check `total_count`

conversation_rating.description: The customer's rating of the conversation, or null: `{rating, remark, created_at, contact, teammate}`

id.description: The conversation id, a decimal string

open.description: True while the conversation is unresolved — **including while it is snoozed**. Use with `state` rather than instead of it

priority.description: `priority` or `not_priority` — Intercom's own two-valued flag, not a severity scale

read.description: Whether a teammate has read it

snoozed_until.description: Unix seconds when a snoozed conversation reopens, or null

source.description: How it started: `{type, id, delivered_as, subject, body, author, attachments}` — the first message, and `author` is who sent it

state.description: The inbox state. `snoozed` is a *kind of open*: see `open` beside it

statistics.description: Timing aggregates — first response time, last close time and so on — or null

tags.description: The paginated wrapper shape — tags at `.data`

teammates.description: The admins on it, same wrapper shape, or null

title.description: The subject, or null — most conversations have none

waiting_since.description: Unix seconds since the customer has been waiting for a reply, or null when they are not. This is the SLA-relevant field

operations.description: Reply to a conversation as an admin. With message_type `comment` the reply is delivered to the end user by email or in-app message and cannot be un-sent; with `note` it is an internal comment only teammates see

params.description: `comment` to reply to the end user, who receives it by email or in-app message, or `note` for an internal comment only teammates see. There is no default: state which audience you mean
params.name: message_type

params.description: The id of the admin the reply is attributed to. The customer sees this teammate's name and avatar, so it must be an admin the operator is entitled to write as
params.name: admin_id

params.description: The reply text as HTML; must not be blank. Intercom renders it in the customer's inbox or messenger
params.name: body

contacts.description: `{type, contacts: […]}` — who the reply went to, when `message_type` was `comment`

conversation_parts.description: WHERE THE SENT REPLY IS: `{type, conversation_parts: […], total_count}`, and the reply is the last entry. Its `part_type` is `comment` (delivered to the customer) or `note` (internal), which is the only confirmation of which audience was written to

created_at.description: Unix seconds — of the conversation, not of this reply

id.description: The conversation's id, unchanged by the reply

open.description: True while unresolved, including while snoozed

source.description: The conversation's first message, not this reply

state.description: The state after the reply. An admin comment on a closed conversation reopens it

updated_at.description: Unix seconds, moved by this reply

waiting_since.description: Null after an admin reply, since the customer is no longer waiting

operations.description: Add an internal note to a contact, visible to teammates in the workspace and never to the contact. Adding the same note twice adds two notes

params.description: The note text as HTML; must not be blank
params.name: body

params.description: The id of the admin the note is attributed to. Intercom treats this as optional; this operation requires it so every note has an author
params.name: admin_id

author.description: The admin it is attributed to: `{type, id, name, email, job_title, away_mode_enabled}`. This is what the required `admin_id` produced

contact.description: The contact it was attached to, as `{type, id}` — **nullable** in Intercom's schema, so confirm it rather than assuming the note landed on a person
